chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, who said:

I and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah were at al-Askar when a messenger came from 'the Man' and said: 'Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ashari, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and Ahmad ibn Hamza ibn al-Yasa are all trusted men.'

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ الْأَشْعَرِي: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ashari (one of the four special deputies)
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: The Man (a title for the Imam during the Ghaybah)
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرُ: Al-Askar (a district near Samarra where the Imams resided)

ai.seo_question: Who are the trusted companions confirmed by the Imam in this narration from al-Askar?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the rigorous chain of transmission used to authenticate the deputies of the Twelfth Imam during the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*). By explicitly naming Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ashari, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and Ahmad ibn Hama ibn al-Yasa as *thiqat*, the text underscores the scholarly consensus on their reliability in conveying the Imam’s directives to the broader community. This verification was crucial for maintaining religious authority and continuity when the Imam was in general concealment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 395 - Ahmad Ibn Idris narrates from Ahmad Ibn Muhammad Ibn Isa from Abu Muhammad Razi, saying:
I and Ahmad Ibn Abi Abdullah were at Askar when a messenger came from “the man” and said: “Ahmad Ibn Ishaq Ashari, Ibrahim Ibn Muhammad Hamadani and Ahmad Ibn Hamza Ibn Yasa are all trusted men.”
